title: Onboarding by Role Kit and Automation Playbook
author: Marina Lopez
body:
Overview:
This playbook describes the standard, role‑based onboarding kits and the automation patterns that People Ops and team stewards use to provision access, tools, and first‑month onboarding experiences at Redwood Inference. It is intended for People Ops, hiring managers, team stewards, and platform engineers who own access automation. The goal is to reduce time‑to‑impact, eliminate ad hoc provisioning, and ensure consistent data/privacy controls across roles.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all newly hired full‑time employees, contractors, and long‑term interns who need access to internal toolchains.
- Excludes short‑term contractors (< 30 days) who are routed through the vendor onboarding checklist.
- Primary audiences: People Ops, Hiring Manager, Team Steward (technical owner), Platform & IT automation engineers.

Objectives and success metrics:
- Average environment and tool access completion within 3 business days for standard roles.
- 95% of new hires completing role‑specific baseline checklist by day 7.
- < 5 support tickets per cohort related to missing permissions after day 7.
- Track metrics in the Onboarding Dashboard (People Ops -> Onboarding -> Access) with automated alerts to owners.

Role Kit taxonomy (high level):
1) Core contributor (IC) kit — default for most engineers, product managers, and analysts:
   - Required accesses: Okta SSO, Redwood Git org (repo list), Slack, Google Workspace, Jira project access, Confluence space contributor.
   - Tool installs: devcontainer template for repo cloning, local GPU driver checklist, Docker, VS Code + extensions.
   - Baseline training: Security Cert A (self‑paced), Data Handling primer (15m), Core API quickstart (30m).

2) Platform/Infra engineer kit:
   - All Core items, plus: cloud console (read-only by default), Terraform state access request form, CI service (runner registration), SSH bastion key enrollment.
   - Automation: infra provisioner job that creates a sandbox project and populates IaC templates.

3) ML/Serving engineer kit:
   - Core + GPU lab access, model serving sandbox on staging, dataset access workflow, secure KMS request template.
   - Quantization/tooling set: conda env YAML, runtime benchmarking script, KV cache debug access (audit gated).

4) Sales / Customer Success kit:
   - Core (limited repo), CRM and case tooling, Redwood Console demo tenant (read‑only), security brief templates for customers.

5) Executive / Restricted kit:
   - Elevated email and calendar, sensitive analytics dashboards (restricted), legal/finance reporting tools, mandatory enhanced MFA (hardware key).

Role kit checklist (canonical items to complete per role):
- Step 0: Offer accepted → Trigger People Ops onboarding workflow (automated webhook to provisioning queue).
- Step 1: Okta account created and MFA enforced (by People Ops).
- Step 2: Git org invite and base repo access (Team Steward).
- Step 3: Slack & Calendar invites + team channels populated (Hiring Manager).
- Step 4: Dev environment template link + local install instructions (Platform).
- Step 5: Role‑specific tool enrolment (e.g., cloud project, KMS) — requires approval ticket where applicable.
- Step 6: First‑week mentor assignment and 30‑60‑90 goals sent (People Ops).

Automation recipes (examples and runbook snippets):
- Provisioning webhook payload (example JSON):
  {
    "full_name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
    "role_kit": "ml-serving-engineer",
    "start_date": "2029-04-01",
    "manager": "leah.kim@redwood.ai"
  }

- CI trigger to create role sandbox (bash):
  # Create project sandbox for new ML engineer
  ./scripts/create-sandbox.sh --project "sandbox-${EMAIL_USERNAME}" --template ml-serving-template || echo "sandbox creation failed"

- Example conda env (roles/ml/envs/ml-serving.yml):
  name: ml-serving-base
  channels: [conda-forge, defaults]
  dependencies:
    - python=3.10
    - numpy
    - pytorch
    - cudatoolkit=12.1

Tool access matrix (table):
Role | Git | Cloud Project | KMS | Customer Data | Console Demo Tenant
-----|-----|---------------|-----|---------------|----------------------
Core | R/W | - (request)   | -   | No            | No
Platform | R/W | Provisioned read/write | Request via ticket | Limited | No
ML Serving | R/W | Provisioned (staging) | Request + approval | Masked (audit) | Yes (staging)
Sales | R | No            | No  | No            | Read‑only
Exec | R/W | Admin (restricted) | Admin (restricted) | Yes (audit) | Yes (prod read)

Numbers above map to gating: "Request" = automated ticket created via /tools/access-request; approval SLA = 2 business days.

30‑Day onboarding timeline (numbered):
1. Day 0 (preboarding): Account creation, welcome email, hardware shipping confirmation, calendar holds created.
2. Day 1: Orientation (People Ops), team intro, dev environment blueprint, first simple task assigned (README update).
3. Days 2–5: Role immersion sessions — paired setup with mentor, access to role kit resources, run baseline smoke tests.
4. Week 2: First project milestone defined, access escalations reviewed, security course completion required.
5. Days 15–30: Feedback checkpoint (People Ops + Manager), productivity blockers triaged, additional tooling access granted if justified.

Onboarding owners and SLAs (table as list):
- People Ops: owner of the main workflow and metrics, SLA: account creation within 1 business day of offer acceptance.
- Platform: owner of devcontainer templates and sandbox provisioning, SLA: sandbox up in 2 days.
- Hiring Manager: team invites and first week plan, SLA: onboarding plan sent within 24 hours of start.
- Team Steward: repo and role permissions, SLA: repo access granted within 2 business days.

Automated alerts and escalation paths:
- If core access incomplete by Day 2, automated Slack alert to People Ops and Hiring Manager.
- If sandbox not provisioned by Day 3, platform oncall notified via PagerDuty.
- If >2 permission tickets opened for a hire after Day 7, People Ops triggers a retrospective with the team steward.

Rollout process for new role kits (how to add/update a kit):
1. Proposal: Team Steward pushes a Role Kit ADR in Confluence with rationale and checklist.
2. Review: People Ops, Platform, and Security reviewers comment (7 business day review window).
3. Automation: If approval granted, Platform implements provisioning automation and a CI test that validates the kit creation.
4. Release: People Ops publishes the kit in the Onboarding Dashboard and updates the role mapping.

Troubleshooting & common issues (runbook):
- Missing Git access: Confirm Okta group sync status, check SCIM logs, escalate to Identity infra.
- Cloud permissions blocked: Verify request ticket was approved; check audit logs for KMS gating.
- Hardware delayed: Interim remote work checklist (VPN, remote dev container).

Security & compliance notes:
- Any role that requests customer data access must include a documented business justification and an approved Data Use Agreement (DUA).
- KMS and key access require manager + security approval; all accesses are logged and rotated per key policy.
- All onboarding automation jobs must run with least privilege service accounts and use short‑lived tokens.

Appendix A — Example onboarding checklist (text checklist for copy/paste):
- [ ] Offer accepted + webhook fired
- [ ] Okta + MFA configured
- [ ] Git org invite accepted
- [ ] Slack + Calendar configured
- [ ] Devcontainer cloned and basic build successful
- [ ] Sandbox project provisioned (if applicable)
- [ ] Security Cert A completed
- [ ] Mentor assigned and 1:1 scheduled

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets and links:
- Access request CLI: /opt/platform/bin/request_access --role ml-serving --email jane.doe@example.com
- Onboarding dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/onboarding
- Automation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-automation

Ownership and maintenance:
- People Ops maintains the playbook content. Platform owns automation templates and CI tests. Team Stewards are responsible for keeping role checklists accurate. Quarterly review cadence: People Ops schedules a review with cross‑functional owners each quarter.

Contact and escalation list:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (primary)
- Platform automation: infra-automation@redwood.ai
- Oncall (Platform): pagerduty.com/redwood/platform

Revision history:
